audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar Balaam spirit-oracles and nations-oracle text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Balaam abandoning enchantments, spirit reception, Mah Tovu tents oracle, Agag/king imagery, third blessing, star-and-scepter oracle, Edom/Amalek/Kenite/Asshur/Kittim nations sayings, and departure.

verses.restored: Balaam saw that it was good in eyes of YHWH to bless Israel, and he did not go as time after time toward enchantments, but set his face toward wilderness.

familiar.text: And when Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he went not, as at other times, to seek for enchantments, but he set his face toward the wilderness.

verses.restored: Balaam lifted his eyes and saw Israel dwelling by its tribes, and spirit of Divine came upon him.

familiar.text: And Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he saw Israel abiding in his tents according to their tribes; and the spirit of God came upon him.

verses.restored: He took up his oracle and said: Declaration of Balaam son of Beor, declaration of man whose eye is opened,

familiar.text: And he took up his parable, and said, Balaam the son of Beor hath said, and the man whose eyes are open hath said:

verses.restored: declaration of one hearing sayings of El, who sees vision of Shaddai, falling down yet with eyes uncovered.

familiar.text: He hath said, which heard the words of God, which saw the vision of the Almighty, falling into a trance, but having his eyes open:

verses.restored: How good are your tents, Jacob, your dwelling-places, Israel!

familiar.text: How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!

verses.restored: Like valleys stretched out, like gardens beside river, like aloes YHWH planted, like cedars beside waters.

familiar.text: As the valleys are they spread forth, as gardens by the river’s side, as the trees of lign aloes which the LORD hath planted, and as cedar trees beside the waters.

verses.restored: Water flows from his buckets, and his seed is in many waters; his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.

familiar.text: He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters, and his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.

verses.restored: El brings him out from Egypt; like horns/strength of wild ox is he for him. He shall consume nations, his adversaries, break their bones, and crush with his arrows.

familiar.text: God brought him forth out of Egypt; he hath as it were the strength of an unicorn: he shall eat up the nations his enemies, and shall break their bones, and pierce them through with his arrows.

verses.restored: He crouches, he lies down like lion and like lioness; who will raise him? Blessed are those blessing you, and cursed are those cursing you.

familiar.text: He couched, he lay down as a lion, and as a great lion: who shall stir him up? Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee.

verses.restored: Anger of Balak burned against Balaam, and he struck his palms together. Balak said to Balaam, To curse my enemies I called you, and look, you have surely blessed these three times.

familiar.text: And Balak’s anger was kindled against Balaam, and he smote his hands together: and Balak said unto Balaam, I called thee to curse mine enemies, and, behold, thou hast altogether blessed them these three times.

verses.restored: Now flee to your place. I said I would honor you greatly, but look, YHWH has held you back from honor.

familiar.text: Therefore now flee thou to thy place: I thought to promote thee unto great honour; but, lo, the LORD hath kept thee back from honour.

verses.restored: Balaam said to Balak, Did I not also speak to your messengers whom you sent to me, saying,

familiar.text: And Balaam said unto Balak, Spake I not also to thy messengers which thou sentest unto me, saying,

verses.restored: If Balak gives me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot cross mouth/command of YHWH to do good or evil from my own heart; what YHWH speaks, that I shall speak?

familiar.text: If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the commandment of the LORD, to do either good or bad of mine own mind; but what the LORD saith, that will I speak?

verses.restored: Now look, I am going to my people. Come, I will counsel/tell you what this people will do to your people in latter days.

familiar.text: And now, behold, I go unto my people: come therefore, and I will advertise thee what this people shall do to thy people in the latter days.

verses.restored: He took up his oracle and said: Declaration of Balaam son of Beor, declaration of man whose eye is opened,

familiar.text: And he took up his parable, and said, Balaam the son of Beor hath said, and the man whose eyes are open hath said:

verses.restored: declaration of one hearing sayings of El and knowing knowledge of Most High, who sees vision of Shaddai, falling down yet with eyes uncovered.

familiar.text: He hath said, which heard the words of God, and knew the knowledge of the most High, which saw the vision of the Almighty, falling into a trance, but having his eyes open:

verses.restored: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star steps forth from Jacob, and a scepter rises from Israel; it shall crush corners of Moab and break down all sons of tumult/Sheth.

familiar.text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.

verses.restored: Edom shall become a possession, Seir shall become possession of its enemies, and Israel shall do valiantly.

familiar.text: And Edom shall be a possession, Seir also shall be a possession for his enemies; and Israel shall do valiantly.

verses.restored: One from Jacob shall rule and destroy survivor from city.

familiar.text: Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion, and shall destroy him that remaineth of the city.

verses.restored: He saw Amalek, took up his oracle, and said: First of nations was Amalek, but his end is destruction.

familiar.text: And when he looked on Amalek, he took up his parable, and said, Amalek was the first of the nations; but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever.

verses.restored: He saw Kenite, took up his oracle, and said: Enduring is your dwelling, and your nest is set in rock.

familiar.text: And he looked on the Kenites, and took up his parable, and said, Strong is thy dwellingplace, and thou puttest thy nest in a rock.

verses.restored: Yet Kain shall be consumed; how long until Asshur carries you captive?

familiar.text: Nevertheless the Kenite shall be wasted, until Asshur shall carry thee away captive.

verses.restored: He took up his oracle and said: Alas, who shall live when El appoints this?

familiar.text: And he took up his parable, and said, Alas, who shall live when God doeth this!

verses.restored: Ships shall come from hand/coast of Kittim; they shall afflict Asshur and afflict Eber, and he also shall come to destruction.

familiar.text: And ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber, and he also shall perish for ever.

verses.restored: Balaam rose and went and returned to his place, and Balak also went his way.

familiar.text: And Balaam rose up, and went and returned to his place: and Balak also went his way.

translation_notes: Balaam abandons his repeated search for enchantments and receives spirit while viewing Israel by tribes; a foreign seer becomes a vehicle of blessing.
'Whose eye is opened' is lexically uncertain and has received multiple interpretations; preserve the ambiguity for audit.
Numbers 24:5, Mah tovu, became a major Jewish liturgical verse. Its Jewish reception must be honored without Christian supersession or appropriation.
Agag may refer to a royal figure or title and requires historical/textual audit.
The star-and-scepter oracle has extensive Jewish, Christian, and political reception history. The restored layer does not collapse it into one later claimant.
Violent domination language toward Moab, Edom, Amalek, and other peoples belongs to ancient royal-war oracle rhetoric and cannot authorize modern ethnic, territorial, or religious violence.
The final nations sayings are compressed and textually difficult, especially Kain, Asshur, Eber, and Kittim.
safety_note: Do not use Numbers 24 to justify ethnic supremacy, conquest, antisemitism, supersessionism, messianic violence, or modern territorial claims. Preserve the beauty of blessing and Jewish liturgical continuity while treating the nations-oracle violence as ancient rhetoric under ethical restraint.
